title: Oxide–Oxide Interactions Dominating the Reaction Pathways in CO2‐Assisted Oxidative Dehydrogenation of Ethane
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The CO
                    2
                    ‐assisted oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane (CO
                    2
                    ‐ODHE) has attracted increasing attention due to the dual benefits of ethylene production and CO
                    2
                    utilization. Among the CO
                    2
                    ‐ODHE catalysts, low‐cost Co‐based catalysts have received special interest recently. However, the complex chemical states of cobalt species lead to competing pathways in CO
                    2
                    ‐ODHE, casting a shadow on their application potential. Herein, we designed two identical‐composition Co
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    ‐ZrO
                    2
                    catalysts with different interfaces and found that the inverse‐structured Co
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    @ZrO
                    2
                    ‐IE synthesized via ion exchange achieved 83% ethylene selectivity; conversely, the traditional supported Co
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    /ZrO
                    2
                    ‐WI prepared by impregnation resulted in primarily CO formation. Comprehensive investigations based on in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations revealed that during the CO
                    2
                    ‐ODHE process, the weaker interfacial oxide–oxide interactions in Co
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    /ZrO
                    2
                    ‐WI made Co
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    readily reduced to metallic Co
                    0
                    , deeply scissoring C─H and C─C bonds, then reacting with O* derived from CO
                    2
                    dissociation, promoting the formation of C
                    2
                    H
                    5
                    O* and CH
                    x
                    * key intermediates leading to ethane dry reforming. Contrastingly, the enhanced oxide–oxide interactions in Co
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    @ZrO
                    2
                    ‐IE inhibited excessive reduction of Co
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    , forming stable interface‐confined Zr–O
                    v
                    –Co
                    2+
                    sites, favored C─H bond activation for the formation of C
                    2
                    H
                    5
                    *, while inhibiting C
                    2
                    H
                    5
                    O* and CH
                    x
                    *, thereby resulting in dehydrogenation to ethylene. This work highlights modulating oxide–oxide interactions as a new strategy for fabricating advanced catalysts.

title: Photocatalytic Isomerization of Stilbenes via Molecular Recognition With a Dual‐Function η6–Arene Catalyst
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes, formed through noncovalent interactions between electron‐rich and electron‐deficient species, can undergo photoinduced charge transfer to access reactive radical intermediates. However, rapid and unproductive back electron transfer (BET) limits their synthetic utility. Herein, we report a dual‐function (
                    η
                    6
                    –arene)rhodium(III) catalyst that enables
                    contra
                    ‐thermodynamic
                    E
                    ‐to‐
                    Z
                    isomerization of stilbenes via selective EDA complexation. In contrast to well‐studied photoisomerization reactions driven by triplet photosensitizers via intermolecular energy transfer (EnT), photoexcitation of the self‐assembled EDA complex generates a charge‐separated singlet exciplex that undergoes back electron transfer coupled with intersystem crossing to populate a localized triplet‐state olefin intermediate. The catalyst plays two pivotal roles: the metal‐bound arene scaffold enables molecular recognition of planar (
                    E
                    )‐stilbenes over twisted (
                    Z
                    )‐isomers through noncovalent interactions, while the heavy rhodium atom promotes ISC.

title: Dynamic Soft‐Confinement via Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks Reshapes C–C Coupling Interfacial Chemistry at Bi1–Bi2 Sites
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The core bottleneck in photocatalytic CO
                    2
                    reduction toward multi‐carbon oxygenates lies in the thermodynamic‐kinetic dual limitations of the C–C coupling step. Conventional strategies have focused on intrinsic electronic structure optimization of active sites while overlooking the critical influence of the reaction microenvironment on coupling probability. Herein, we propose a dynamic soft‐confinement catalytic strategy by in situ constructing a disordered hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF) layer on Bi
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    Br surfaces, thereby establishing an HOF/Bi
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    Br integrated photocatalytic system. The introduction of HOF not only induces the formation of asymmetric Bi
                    1
                    –Bi
                    2
                    coupling sites but also establishes a dynamic hydrogen‐bonding microenvironment surrounding them. This microenvironment enhances CO
                    2
                    coverage near the coupling sites by constructing a persistent carbon source enrichment layer. Simultaneously, the interfacial polarization field promotes exciton dissociation and directs electron transport toward the Bi
                    1
                    –Bi
                    2
                    sites. Furthermore, the reconfigurable hydrogen bonds impose orientational soft confinement on *CO intermediates, guiding them into spatial configurations favorable for *OCCO bond formation. This soft‐hard synergistic interfacial design enables 0.7HOF/Bi
                    3
                    O
                    4
                    Br to achieve a CH
                    3
                    COOH production rate of 325.12 µmol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    with 98.81% product selectivity under sacrificial agent‐free conditions. This work demonstrates that dynamic microenvironment programming around active sites constitutes a critical pathway for overcoming the photocatalytic C–C coupling bottleneck.

title: Spatially Decoupled Charge Compensation Enables Versatile Cation–Anion Co‐Intercalation in Layered Metal Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Multivalent cation–anion co‐(de)intercalation offers a promising pathway to higher energy densities in multivalent ion batteries. However, its practical realization is challenged by lattice strain and the lack of effective dual charge‐compensation strategies. Here, we report a layered vanadium oxide cathode with pre‐intercalated melamine ligands (MeVO) that enables a spatially decoupled charge‐compensation mechanism—organic ligands serve as redox centers for anions, while metal sites accommodate multivalent cation redox. This design alleviates electrostatic crowding, promotes ion mobility, and preserves structural integrity. Using Mg
                    2
                    +
                    ‐TFSI
                    −
                    as a representative system, MeVO delivers a record cycle life of over 36 000 cycles at a loading of approximately 3 mg cm
                    −
                    2
                    and an areal capacity of 3.3 mAh cm
                    −
                    2
                    at a higher loading of 16.4 mg cm
                    −
                    2
                    , surpassing leading Mg‐ion cathodes. The hybrid structure also supports co‐(de)intercalation of various multivalent cations and anions, demonstrating its potential as a versatile intercalation platform for high‐performance energy storage.

title: Development of a Potent QS‐21‐Derived Adjuvant Photoaffinity Probe: Identification of Cathepsin D as the Molecular Receptor
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The saponin natural product QS‐21 is a potent immunological adjuvant used in human vaccines to enhance the immune response but suffers from scarcity, instability, and dose‐limiting toxicity, precluding its advancement as a stand‐alone adjuvant. Further, putative cellular receptor(s) and its molecular mechanisms of action are unknown, which has prevented the rational design of saponin adjuvants, emphasizing the need for discovering these receptors and elucidating mechanisms. Herein, we have developed novel saponin photoaffinity probes for molecular target identification, merging synthetic chemistry, photoaffinity labeling, and chemical proteomics. One of these potent adjuvants generated superior antibody responses to QS‐21 with less toxicity and enabled identification of Cathepsin D (CatD) as the selective receptor driving saponin adjuvant effects. Binding to surface‐exposed CatD, lipid raft interactions, and lysosomal acidification were shown to be key for CatD‐mediated saponin‐induced immune activation, whereas neither photocrosslinking nor apparent binding was observed in comparative experiments with other lysosomal cathepsins, confirming the specificity of the interaction. These studies highlight the promise of this saponin probe as a potent vaccine adjuvant, unveiling CatD as the molecular target. This breakthrough sets the stage for elucidating the precise mechanisms of saponin immunopotentiation, facilitating rational adjuvant design and development of optimized adjuvant–antigen combinations for future vaccines.

title: Smart Piezoelectric Hybrid Ceramic Membrane With the Capacity of Pulsed Responsive Self‐Cleaning and Anti‐Fouling Functions
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic fouling remains a major challenge for ceramic membrane filtration because of the strong adsorption of organic foulants on membrane surfaces. Herein, a novel design strategy is proposed for smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes featuring self‐powered nano‐brushes. Specifically, a self‐powered nano‐brush smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membrane (ATPAA
                    −
                    ‐PBM) with the pulsed pressure responsiveness and self‐cleaning capability was prepared by grafting negatively charged sodium PAA polymer chain (PAA
                    −
                    ) on the surface of BaTiO
                    3
                    (BTO) piezoelectric ceramic membrane. Under the pulsed pressure, alternating piezoelectric charges induced reversible conformational oscillations of the self‐powered nano‐brushes, promoting the detachment of the foulant layer by the flowing water and thereby enabling in situ self‐cleaning. Meanwhile, the grafted PAA
                    −
                    nano‐brushes strongly associated with water molecules to establish a 462 nm‐thick hydration layer, while generating electrostatic repulsion toward humic acid (HA), jointly preventing foulant adhesion and enabling nearly complete rejection. The membrane exhibited outstanding retention, anti‐fouling ability, and remarkable flux retention ratio (FRR = 92.3%, 10 d) during a long‐term filtration process. Consequently, a novel excellent rejection and anti‐fouling mechanism of “self‐powered nano‐brush dynamic oscillation self‐cleaning & hydration barrier” was proposed. This study provides a new perspective for the fabrication of self‐cleaning smart piezoelectric hybrid ceramic membranes.

title: Oxygen‐Coordinated Nickel Single Atoms Couple Photohole Capture With C–H Cleavage in Photoelectrocatalytic Glycerol‐to‐Dihydroxyacetone Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Selective photoelectrochemical oxidation of glycerol to dihydroxyacetone (DHA) requires photogenerated holes to reach the substrate faster than they drive oxygen evolution, followed by C–H cleavage without C–C fragmentation. Here, oxygen‐coordinated Ni single atoms on the TiO
                    2
                    (001) nanosheet arrays regulate both steps. Isopropanol‐probe and in situ glycerol spectra support Ni‐promoted dissociative adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group. Radical spectroscopy and interfacial kinetics support subsequent oxidation through glycerol‐derived alkoxy species, accompanied by a 15–20‐fold acceleration of glycerol‐coupled hole transfer and suppressed oxygen evolution. Product‐based glycerol isotope effects supported the kinetic involvement of central C–H cleavage in DHA formation, while calculations showed that Ni coordination increased the energetic preference for C–H over C–C cleavage from 0.05 to 0.38 eV. Operando spectroscopy and weaker DHA adsorption support retention of the three‐carbon skeleton and product release. Under charge‐normalized conditions, the Ni single‐atom photoanode achieved a DHA Faradaic efficiency of approximately 66.6%, compared with 22.2% for unmodified TiO
                    2
                    and 16.4% for the NiO
                    x
                    control. DHA‐selective charge utilization persisted in recirculating‐flow operation with 0.5 M glycerol. These results support coupled control over substrate adsorption and subsequent bond selectivity as a design principle for selective PEC polyol oxidation.

title: Bromide–Borate Coupling Enables Selective Electrochemical Oxidation of Glycerol to Dihydroxyacetone
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Selective electrochemical valorization of biodiesel‐derived glycerol is challenged by competing oxidation pathways that generate complex product mixtures. Here, we report a bromide–borate‐mediated indirect glycerol electrooxidation for selective dihydroxyacetone (DHA) production on carbon electrodes. Bromide is electrochemically converted into soluble oxidized bromine species that mediate homogeneous glycerol oxidation, whereas borate provides a weakly alkaline bromine‐speciation window and coordinates glycerol to bias C3‐product formation toward DHA. At identical pH, borate favored DHA formation, whereas phosphate shifted selectivity toward glyceric acid. Under optimized conditions using 100 mM glycerol and 100 mM KBr in 1 M borate buffer solution (pH 8.2), divided H‐cell electrolysis afforded DHA with 75% relative selectivity and high overall Faradaic efficiency (FE). Recirculating flow‐cell operation increased DHA selectivity to 80% while maintaining high overall FE, and one‐way flow‐cell achieved a DHA production rate of 1205 mmol m
                    −2 
                    h
                    −1
                    .

title: Topology‐Derived Closed Pores in Hard Carbon Boost Sodium‐Ion Storage
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The closed‐pore architecture of hard carbon governs reversible capacity, initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), and Na‐storage kinetics, but its precise regulation and the underlying mechanism remain elusive. To address such issues, a molecular‐cavity engineering strategy is developed using cyclic molecular precursors, whose inherent cavities are preserved by low‐temperature cross‐linking, to construct topology‐derived intrinsic closed pores in hard carbon during carbonization. Using β‐cyclodextrin as a model precursor, the resulting hard carbon (β‐ICHC) delivers a reversible capacity of 410.2 mAh g
                    −1
                    , an ICE of 94.7% and 99.7% capacity retention over 300 cycles. Combined theoretical and in situ/ex situ analyses reveal that intrinsic closed pores simultaneously enable high reversible capacity, high ICE, and fast Na‐storage kinetics: the intrinsic closed pores with sub‐0.35 nm electrolyte‐sieving mouths can not only serve as reversible Na‐storage spaces to increase capacity but also suppress irreversible Na
                    +
                    consumption to enhance ICE; the pseudo‐graphitic walls with enlarged interlayer spacing enable fast Na
                    +
                    transport and provide additional capacity. Furthermore, a three‐stage Na‐storage mechanism of surface/defect adsorption, closed‐pore‐wall adsorption, and closed‐pore filling is supported by the combined experimental and theoretical results. This work provides a paradigm for hard‐carbon structural design and offers new insight into sodium‐storage mechanisms.

title: Bimetallic Coinage Metal Complexes of Tetradentate ortho‐Ter‐arylene Ligands
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    We report a series of photoluminescent bimetallic Cu(I), Ag(I), and Au(I) complexes supported by tetradentate donor‐acceptor ligands containing two monoanionic amide donors (D) and two aza‐arene acceptors (A). The metal complexes of the ligand containing carbazolide and pyridyl ligating groups possess high photoluminescence quantum yields (up to 65% in solution) and emission properties consistent with thermally‐activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Bimetallic Cu(I) complexes of similar ligands containing benzannulated donor (benzo[a]carbazolide) or acceptor (isoquinoline) moieties demonstrate that absorption/emission properties are tunable by modification of D/A groups. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction of the bimetallic complexes reveals metal–metal distances shorter than the sum of their van der Waals radii, suggesting metallophilic interactions between the d
                    10
                    metal centers. Ultrafast excited‐state kinetic analysis reveals nearly equal exergonic intersystem crossing rates between Cu(I) and Au(I) complexes, contrary to what is expected from each metal's spin–orbit coupling contributions. These findings are corroborated with theoretical modeling, which suggests that the optical transitions of these bimetallic complexes are characterized as metal–ligand‐to‐ligand charge transfer (MLLCT) states.

title: pH‐Driven Two‐Stage Conformational Switching Activates an Acid‐Responsive Chaperone
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Acidification rapidly denatures bacterial periplasmic proteins, yet this compartment lacks ATP‐dependent chaperones. We identify AchC as an acid‐responsive, ATP‐independent chaperone crucial for acid tolerance in
                    Pseudomonas aeruginosa
                    . As proton influx across the outer membrane leaves insufficient time for transcriptional or translational adaptation, AchC is activated post‐translationally. We reveal that AchC is activated by precisely tuned, conformational transitions driven by pH changes. At neutral pH, AchC is maintained as an inactive dimer. Upon acidification, it undergoes two structural transitions: C‐terminal conformational loosening under mildly acidic conditions (pH 4.0–5.5), followed by complete monomerization under severe acid stress (pH ≤ 3.0) to fully activate its substrate‐holding function. Once activated, AchC exhibits potent anti‐aggregation activity across a broad spectrum of substrates. Upon neutralization, AchC releases its substrates in refolding‐competent state in ATP‐independent manner. In vivo, the deletion of
                    achC
                    increases acid susceptibility, whereas its overexpression confers acid tolerance. Furthermore, this chaperone is important for biofilm formation, motility, and pathogenicity. Our findings demonstrate how this dynamic molecular remodeling directly couples environmental sensing to bacterial survival.

title: Identifying a Langmuir–Hinshelwood Hydrogenation Mechanism to Design a Bimetallic AgPd Catalyst for Electrochemical Acetylene‐to‐Ethylene Conversion
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The intensified hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) competition is an elusive obstacle for the practical application of electrocatalytic acetylene (C
                    2
                    H
                    2
                    ) hydrogenation (EAH) for petroleum‐independent ethylene (C
                    2
                    H
                    4

Fundamentally, ambiguous mechanistic insight severely hinders the rational design of efficient catalysts, leaving the identification of Eley–Rideal (E–R) or Langmuir–Hinshelwood (L–H) mechanisms as intrinsic challenges. Here, the L–H pathway is proven to be the predominant route, which is regarded as the principle for catalyst design. Consequently, a bimetallic AgPd alloy (AgPd NPs) is predicted and proven to be a promising catalyst. Accordingly, the AgPd NPs deliver a C
                    2
                    H
                    4
                    partial current density of 0.47 A cm
                    −2
                    and a turnover frequency (TOF) of 8.27 s
                    −1
                    (1.66‐fold vs. the Ag counterpart under equal conditions). In situ spectroscopic characterizations unveil that the Pd dopants could not only induce *H transfer to free sites to increase C
                    2
                    H
                    2
                    mass transfer, but also optimize the match degree of surface *H and *C
                    2
                    H
                    2

                    2
                    H
                    4

title: Dimensional Reduction of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides by Oxide Insertion: Quasi‐1D Oxychalcogenide Semiconductors
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Heteroanionic solids offer unique levers for tuning structures and properties, but accessing multianion phase space remains challenging due to mismatches in anion reactivity. Here, we describe a new family of A
                    2
                    Hf
                    3
                    Q
                    6
                    O (A = K, Rb, Cs; Q = S, Se) oxychalcogenides, the first reported in the A─Hf─Q─O quaternary space, which are prepared by reacting HfQ
                    2
                    with the corresponding alkali carbonate (A
                    2
                    CO
                    3
                    ). The resulting structures are dimensionally reduced variants of the 1T‐HfQ
                    2
                    parent phase, where rows of O atoms insert into the transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) layers. This yields nanometer‐wide 1D‐[Hf
                    3
                    Q
                    6
                    ] ribbons that link into step‐like sheets through distinctive Hf─O─Hf bridges, which connect heteroleptic HfQ
                    5
                    O polyhedra at the ribbon edges. UV/Vis and photoluminescence spectra reveal tunable absorption and emission features spanning 1.8–2.6 eV. Calculated band structures show direct‐gap transitions and highly dispersive bands along the [Hf
                    3
                    Q
                    6
                    ] nanoribbons, yielding effective masses more than two orders of magnitude lower than in other crystallographic directions. Charge‐density plots further illustrate quasi‐1D electronic anisotropy, showing frontier orbitals confined to the nanoribbons due to covalent Hf─Q bonding. We anticipate heteroanion‐driven dimensional reduction can be used to engineer anisotropy in semiconductors and offers new routes to synthetically challenging multianion systems.

title: Machine Learning in Liquid Electrolyte Design for Rechargeable Batteries: Addressing Fundamental Challenges
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Designing high‐performance liquid electrolytes for rechargeable batteries requires simultaneously achieving fast ionic transport, a wide electrochemical window, and interphase stability, yet these objectives are intrinsically coupled and often involve competing trade‐offs. Electrolyte optimization remains a formidable challenge for conventional trial‐and‐error approaches. Recent advances in machine learning (ML) are transforming electrolyte research into a data‐driven and increasingly autonomous paradigm for accelerated materials discovery. This review provides a comprehensive perspective on how ML methodologies are tailored to address the fundamental challenges of liquid electrolyte design. We first introduce the physicochemical foundations of liquid electrolytes alongside key ML workflows, emphasizing dataset construction and feature representation tailored to electrolyte chemistry. We then examine ML strategies for predicting and optimizing ionic transport, electrochemical window, interphase regulation, and multi‐objective optimization, highlighting representative advances and practical design principles for rational electrolyte development. Finally, we discuss current challenges, including data quality, model generalizability, and interpretability, as well as future opportunities for developing mechanism‐informed and transferable ML frameworks. By bridging machine learning with electrolyte science, this review aims to facilitate the rational design of next‐generation liquid electrolytes and accelerate the development of high‐performance rechargeable batteries.

title: Synergy Between Controllable Sulfur Defect and NiS Cocatalyst Enabling Efficient Photoredox Coupling Catalysis
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Semiconductor‐based photoredox coupling of selective oxidation of vanillyl alcohol (VOL) to vanillin (VAL) with H
                    2
                    evolution provides a sustainable alternative to conventional industrial VAL synthesis processes, yet its performance is often hindered by rapid charge recombination and insufficient active sites. Herein, we report a facile one‐pot hydrothermal strategy to construct NiS‐decorated Zn
                    3
                    In
                    2
                    S
                    6
                    (ZIS) nanoflowers with controllable sulfur vacancies (V
                    S
                    ) for efficient co‐production of VAL and H
                    2
                    . Moderate concentrations of V
                    S
                    regulate the surface electronic structure and act as oxidation active sites to optimize VOL adsorption. Meanwhile, uniformly dispersed NiS cocatalysts serve as efficient electron relays and reduction active sites, accelerating charge migration and promoting H
                    2
                    generation. Benefiting from the interfacial synergy between V
                    S
                    and NiS, the optimal 1%NiS‐ZIS‐V
                    S2
                    catalyst delivers an 18‐fold enhancement in both VAL and H
                    2
                    production rates relative to pristine ZIS, together with excellent stability and broad substrate versatility. This work highlights the critical role of defect‐cocatalyst synergy in designing advanced cooperative photoredox catalysts for sustainable chemical synthesis.

title: Engineering Advanced Electrocatalysts for Energy‐Saving Zinc−Air Hybrid Batteries: Concurrent Energy Storage Coupled With Chemical Upgrading
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Additive‐assisted zinc−air hybrid batteries (ZAHBs) that couple favorable additive oxidation with oxygen reduction represent ideal energy storage candidates, distinguished by high theoretical energy density, reduced charging voltage, and functionality for electrochemical upgrading of organics or wastewater. Herein, a critical overview of ZAHBs is provided, commencing with the fundamental electrochemistry (including advantages, working mechanisms, cell configurations, and evaluation parameters) and the selection criteria for small‐molecule additives (including theoretical potential, solubility, stability, toxicity, and volatility). We then summarize recent progress in three categories of ZAHBs (i.e., wastewater‐purified, value‐added, and redox‐mediated), discussing alternative anodic oxidation reactions (e.g., alcohol, urea, hydrazine, and iodine oxidation) coupled with cathodic oxygen reduction, along with the underlying catalytic mechanisms. Particular emphasis is placed on catalyst design strategies spanning electronic (ligand engineering, heteroatom doping, electron delocalization, orbital hybridization, and built‐in electric field), geometric (defect engineering, curvature engineering, and nano‐confinement effect), and interfacial (high‐energy interface, heterostructure, interfacial microenvironment, and core–shell structure) modulations. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and future perspectives for advancing ZAHBs. This review offers valuable guidance for the rational design and practical deployment of next‐generation energy devices.

title: Site‐Selectively Engineered MoS2/ReS2 Heterostructures for High‐Performance Supercapacitors
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Layered MoS
                    2
                    holds great potential for supercapacitors; however, its intrinsically low electrical conductivity, sluggish electrochemical kinetics, and susceptibility to Mo dissolution severely hamper its electrochemical performance. Here, we propose a selective‐doping‐coupled heterostructure engineering strategy, in which atomic Fe preferentially incorporates into the MoS
                    2
                    domain, while the local structure of the ReS
                    2

title: Ligand Electronics and Metal‐Site Acidity Enable High‐Voltage MOF Electrolytes for Quasi‐Solid‐State Lithium‐Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium‐metal batteries (LMBs) coupled with Ni‐rich cathodes offer high energy density for next‐generation energy storage. Their practical implementation, however, is limited by electrolyte oxidation and interfacial degradation under high voltage. Metal‐organic frameworks (MOFs) would regulate ion solvation and stabilize electrode‐electrolyte interfaces in quasi‐solid‐state electrolytes, yet the molecular origins of their oxidation stability remain unclear. Here, we identify ligand electronics and metal‐site acidity as key descriptors for high‐voltage‐stable MOF electrolytes. Electron‐withdrawing ligands lower the HOMO energy levels of MOFs, while hard Lewis‐acidic Al sites further enhance oxidation resistance. Guided by this principle, we design a perfluorinated Al‐based MOF, Al‐FBDC, featuring a high oxidation onset potential of 4.82 V (vs. Li
                    +
                    /Li). Incorporating Al‐FBDC into a composite cathode reconstructs the local electrolyte environment at particle‐level interfaces, thereby suppressing parasitic reactions and cathode degradation under high‐voltage operation. As a result, Li||Al‐FBDC@NCM quasi‐solid‐state cells deliver excellent long‐term cycling stability and rate performance, retaining 82% of the capacity after 200 cycles at 1 C over 3.0‐4.5 V, while maintaining robust performance even at 4.6 and 4.8 V cut‐off voltages and with controlled electrolyte loading. This work identifies a general design principle for high‐voltage‐stable MOF electrolytes and offers a practical route toward high‐energy‐density LMBs.

source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic photocatalysts with tailored properties and unique processability offer a sustainable route to solar hydrogen. To maximize light harvesting and charge generation, donor and acceptor materials are usually physically mixed to form D:A heterojunction nanoparticles (NPs). However, weakly constrained interactions can promote phase segregation, morphological evolution, and limited reproducibility. Here, we introduce an all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymer, PBDB‐T‐
                    b

These results establish all‐conjugated donor–acceptor block copolymers as a promising design strategy for combining high activity, operational stability, and reproducibility in organic nanoparticle photocatalysis.

title: Stress‐Resistant Plant Cell‐Wall Inspired Cell Armor Enables Red Blood Cell Lyophilization
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lyophilization offers an attractive route for ambient‐temperature storage of biological systems by eliminating cold‐chain dependence and suppressing solution‐phase degradation. However, lyophilizing mammalian cells remains challenging due to their vulnerability to coupled stresses, including ice‐induced mechanical injury and membrane destabilization during freezing and dehydration. In nature, stress‐resistant plant cells survive extreme conditions through multifunctional cell walls. Inspired by their natural survival strategies, we engineer an artificial membrane armor (AMA) that enables efficient lyophilization of red blood cells (RBCs). This biomimetic AMA integrates a nanoporous zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF‐8) for mechanical support, a water‐retentive polymer matrix for hydration retention and colloidal stabilization, and Zn
                    2
                    +
                    coordination preserves membrane fluidity and suppresses freeze‐ and dehydration‐driven membrane phase transitions. Through synergistic interfacial protection, the AMA effectively buffers coupled stresses associated with lyophilization, enabling ∼95% post‐rehydration recovery of RBCs using an ultra‐low protectant content (<5 wt%) together with an ambient shelf‐life of at least 3 months, unachievable with previous methods. Furthermore, the rehydrated RBCs preserve their native morphology, membrane mechanics, metabolic activity, oxygen transport capability, and in vivo circulation behavior. This work establishes a bioinspired interfacial engineering strategy for transferring desiccation tolerance from plants to mammalian cells, advancing ambient‐temperature biostorage of sensitive living systems.

title: Cortex-wide imaging in naturally behaving mice with 1-gram wireless mesoscopes
source: Nature
abstract: Revealing how distributed cortical circuits coordinate behavior in freely moving animals remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience, constrained by limited fields of view, low throughput, and the tethering required by current miniaturized microscopes1-4. Here, we present Airscope, a wireless mesoscope delivering 4 μm lateral resolution across a 6 mm field of view at 12.5 Hz, weighing 1.0 gram. An aspheric-lens design achieves a 2.84× shorter total track length than previous miniaturized microscopes1,2,5,6 while matching the neuron yield of benchtop one-photon mesoscopes; a tailored wireless link supports cable-free calcium imaging from >8,500 neurons per animal (25‑fold increase). Paired with a zero-shot behavior analyzer, Airscope enables cortical imaging across rich behavioral conditions, including room-scale enriched arenas, swimming assays, and multi-organ implantation, with concurrent recording from multiple animals. Using Airscope, we demonstrate versatile applications of untethered cortical imaging across diverse behavioral paradigms. We identify cortical activity patterns across multiple dorsal regions that correlate with behavioral signatures of social dominance, and show dorsal-cortical population activity prospectively decodes competition outcomes across paired animals. We observe reward-location-associated cortical activity patterns during maze exploration, and characterize Granger-causal influence from spinal cord to cortex during fear conditioning, enabled by simultaneous brain-spinal recordings. By uniting large-scale, cellular-resolution recording with unconstrained behavior, Airscope makes naturalistic, multi-animal cortical recording experimentally practical, and provides a broadly accessible technology for systems neuroscience.

title: Ligand-protected copper nanoclusters enable room-temperature semihydrogenation of terminal alkynes
source: Chem
abstract: An atomically precise, ligand-capped Cu49 nanocluster is demonstrated to efficiently catalyze the semihydrogenation of alkynes at room temperature. Its unique surface coordination architecture governs substrate adsorption via steric effects; this structural feature, combined with the cluster’s remarkable stability, concurrently facilitates effective alkyne activation and ensures high hydrogenation selectivity. Notably, this work overcomes the conventional dependence on noble metals such as gold and palladium in hydrogenation catalysis, revealing the significant potential of ligand-protected copper nanoclusters for this transformation.

title: Bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnets enable untethered organ monitoring
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Metal-free molecular magnets differ from conventional magnetic devices that predominantly rely on metallic magnets as these metal-free materials may offer biocompatibility and bioresorbability. However, existing molecular materials lack the ferromagnetic strength required for high-fidelity sensing at clinically relevant tissue depths. Here we introduce a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet derived from graphitic carbon nitride, combining metallic-level ferromagnetism with full bioresorbability. De-nitrogenation creates spin centres coupled through a reconstructed π–σ conjugated framework, conferring robust spontaneous magnetization that remains stable under physiological conditions. Integrated with poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) and silk fibroin, the material forms catheter-deliverable epicardial patches for cardiac tracking and can also be dispersed in injectable hydrogels for organ-scale sensing, including the three-dimensional reconstruction of localized hepatic pathologies. Coupled with a skin-interfaced Hall array, this magnetic sensing architecture provides the continuous, untethered monitoring of multi-organ dynamics, robust against motion artifacts and tissue impedance. In porcine models, it facilitates the continuous assessment of ejection fraction over 4 weeks, followed by benign bioresorption. Benchmarked against standard-of-care echocardiography, this approach delivers clinical-grade trajectories, supporting longitudinal, infrastructure-independent physiological monitoring.

title: Cost-driven strategies towards industrially manufacturable perovskite photovoltaics
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: With power conversion efficiencies exceeding 27%, perovskite solar cells (PSCs) are transitioning from laboratory-scale efficiency-driven research to a focus on large-scale deployment. At this stage, manufacturing cost is emerging as a key constraint governing the industrial competitiveness of PSCs. The manufacturing cost of PSCs (approximately US$0.3–0.6 W−1) remains much higher than that of mature crystalline silicon solar cells (approximately $0.1 W−1); therefore, it is essential to incorporate cost considerations into the future technological development of PSCs. In this Review, we discuss advances in PSC research from a cost-driven perspective, organized into three dimensions: enhancing manufacturing yield by addressing material reliability and process tolerance, reducing material costs by rethinking material selection and device architectures alongside material recycling strategies, and simplifying fabrication by alleviating dependence on controlled environments, specialized equipment and energy-intensive processing. Finally, we discuss how cost-oriented principles can be incorporated into PSC research and development while maintaining competitive device performance to facilitate their transition from laboratory studies to commercially viable photovoltaic technologies.

title: Elevating CO2 electrolyzer temperature accelerates the viability of chemical electrification
source: Nature Chemical Engineering
abstract: Climate change mitigation has spurred interest in producing chemicals from CO2. CO2 reduction by electrochemistry can be driven directly by green electricity, yielding even multi-carbon (C2+) products. However, the resulting processes still suffer from high electrolyzer losses and substantial energy demands. This study evaluates the environmental and economic benefits of integrating optimized electrolyzers into complete processes. For CO2 electroreduction to ethylene and dimerization to 1-butene, elevated-temperature electrolysis effectively utilizes waste heat. Challenging the ambient-temperature paradigm, this strategy achieves system-wide savings in energy (10%), climate impacts (9%) and overall cost (11%). Generalizing these findings across various CO2 electroreduction pathways identifies energy savings of up to 25% and the heating system as a key design variable affecting electrolyzer design targets. Our study demonstrates how process integration can guide CO2 electrolyzer development toward sustainable processes.

title: Water serves as a charge-transfer medium for ultrafast aqueous batteries
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: Charge storage in aqueous batteries is commonly understood through an ion-centric picture, in which metal ions or pre-existing protons transport and compensate charge. However, conventional metal-ion diffusion and proton insertion do not fully account for seconds-level kinetics, strong cation–electrode specificity and experimentally detectable proton signatures observed at the low equilibrium proton concentrations in aqueous metal-ion batteries. In this Perspective, we propose that interfacial water can serve as a charge-transfer medium under certain conditions, with ultrafast kinetics arising from the cleavage and reorganization of water at electrode–electrolyte interfaces. In this framework, water-derived protons provide charge compensation through insertion processes, and the formation and relaxation of short-lived water-derived intermediates reflect the activation of water cleavage. We outline the working principles of ultrafast charging behaviour mediated by interfacial water and its positioning among known fast charging pathways in aqueous batteries, the physical origin and tunability of interfacial water cleavage, and transient spectroscopic tools capable of resolving the evolution of short-lived water-derived intermediates. Finally, we discuss the implications of this interfacial-water-centred view for electrode and device design and for high-power aqueous energy-storage applications.

title: Analogue fast Fourier transforms for scalable and efficient signal processing
source: Nature Electronics
abstract: Edge devices are increasingly being deployed to sense and act on information from the physical world. The discrete Fourier transform is widely used to make these sensed data suitable for further processing and transmission over communication networks. Analogue in-memory computing can provide energy-efficient processing at the edge, particularly for artificial intelligence workloads, but it has not been extended to large Fourier transforms. This is because modern signal processing relies on the fast Fourier transform algorithm to reduce the computational complexity of discrete Fourier transforms, but the fast Fourier transform has remained restricted to digital processors. Here we show that the fast Fourier transform can be efficiently mapped to analogue in-memory computing systems, allowing them to scale to arbitrarily large transforms without requiring impractically large or numerous non-volatile memory arrays. We experimentally demonstrate analogue fast Fourier transforms on one-dimensional audio and two-dimensional image signals, performing precise analogue computations across up to 524k charge-trapping memory devices simultaneously within one array. We use this approach to compute analogue Fourier transforms of up to 65,536 points.

title: Robust Dipicolinic Acid‐Anchored Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Wide‐Bandgap and Tandem Perovskite Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The anchoring group of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) hole‐transporting materials dictates both substrate binding and interfacial passivation, serving as a key lever for high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics. Herein, we report a novel SAM molecular material,
                    denoted by
                    XS21
                    , engineered with a multidentate dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchoring core to address conventional adhesion and degradation limitations. From an experimental perspective, the DPA anchor is found to promote molecular chemisorption onto the substrate, potentially originating from the dual‐action mechanism of pyridine–Ni coordination coupled with dicarboxylate‐metal interaction. Furthermore,
                    XS21
                    imparts both low acid‐dissociation constants (
                    K
                    a
                    ) and superior ultraviolet (UV) photostability. Consequently, wide‐bandgap (1.79 eV) perovskite solar cells containing
                    XS21
                    deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.54% with an exceptional open‐circuit voltage of 1.372 V. Crucially, integrating
                    XS21
                    into monolithic all‐perovskite tandem solar cells yields a remarkable PCE of 29.62%, alongside an outstanding operational stability (retaining >90% of initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation). This work establishes multi‐dentate pyridine‐carboxylate anchoring as a vital paradigm for next‐generation efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Breaking the Boltzmann Limit: A Review of Emerging Ultralow‐Power Transistor Technologies
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  As complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor (CMOS) technology scales down to the sub‐2 nm node, the dramatic surge in power density has emerged as a fundamental bottleneck. Conventional metal‐oxide‐semiconductor field‐effect transistors (MOSFETs) are constrained by the 60 mV/dec Boltzmann thermal limit, rendering further supply voltage reduction exceedingly challenging. To surmount this fundamental limit, various novel sub‐60 mV/dec steep‐switching devices have been proposed, including tunnel field‐effect transistors (TFETs), negative‐capacitance field‐effect transistors (NCFETs), and cold‐source field‐effect transistors (CSFETs). A comprehensive review of the evolution of sub‑60 mV/dec technologies is presented, with particular emphasis on the three mainstream approaches: TFETs, NCFETs, and CSFETs. The underlying physical principles, recent research advances, optimization strategies, and remaining challenges of these devices are thoroughly analyzed. Finally, prospective directions for future breakthroughs are discussed, encompassing novel materials exploration, the synergistic integration of multiple physical mechanisms, and the experimental verification of integration with advanced CMOS nodes.

title: Robust Spin Splitting and Fermiology in the Layered Altermagnet CoNb4${\rm CoNb}_4$Se8${\rm Se}_8$
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum‐dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three‐dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination‐resolved micro‐ARPES, fine photon‐energy mapping, spin‐ARPES, and density functional theory, we map the three‐dimensional fermiology of the layered
                    g
                    ‐wave altermagnet , obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H‐. We resolve the spin–split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin‐ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time‐reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry‐protected nodal –K direction. We further report a weak low‐temperature anomaly near
                    T
                    0
                     ≈ 50–60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature‐dependent micro‐ARPES, and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum‐resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.

title: Disentangling Polaron Formation Pathways in Y6 by Probing Noninteracting and Interacting Chromophores via Transient Absorption Spectroscopy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  In highly efficient organic solar cells, the optoelectronic properties of the non‐fullerene acceptor Y6 are governed by the molecular packing of noninteracting and interacting molecules. In this study, steady‐state and transient absorption spectroscopy are employed to disentangle the spectral signatures and excited‐state dynamics of interacting and noninteracting Y6 in solution and thin films. By controlling aggregation in dilute solution, we identify localized Frenkel‐type excitons (LE) on noninteracting Y6 and aggregate excitons (AE) on intermolecular interacting Y6. The AEs exhibit strongly fluence‐dependent lifetimes (30–200 ps) governed by singlet–singlet annihilation, whereas localized excitons decay monoexponentially on a nanosecond timescale. Furthermore, long‐lived polaronic states are observed to form on aggregated Y6 within tens of picoseconds and persist into the nanosecond regime. Comparison with thin‐film measurements reveals similar processes with an additional ultrafast energy transfer from noninteracting chromophores to aggregated domains. These results establish a consistent framework for assigning transient absorption features in Y6 and suggest that, in neat films of Y6, the pairwise formation of polarons arises from an Onsager‐like autoionization process of delocalized excitons in domains of interacting Y6 with moderate yield. This provides central insight into charge‐generation mechanisms in Y6‐based photovoltaic systems.

title: Durable Interphase Incorporating Cross‐Linked Polymer Enables Long‐Calendar‐Life Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The practical deployment of lithium (Li) metal batteries is hindered by not only cycle life but also calendar life. The poor calendar life stems from both the repeated reconstruction of the solid‐electrolyte interphase (SEI) during cycles and, particularly, the continuous growth of SEI during storage. Herein, a durable SEI with high mechanical stability against volume fluctuations and superior passivation capability to suppress electrolyte permeation is demonstrated by integrating inorganics and a cross‐linked polymer into the SEI. Concretely, a cross‐linked polymer with high modulus and low swelling is in‐situ incorporated among the inorganics of an anion‐derived SEI. The elastic modulus of the SEI is significantly increased from 1.63 to 4.37 GPa, and the compactness of the SEI is also improved to suppress electrolyte permeation. Consequently, the cycle life and calendar life of Li metal coin cells are extended by 73% (from 190 to 329 cycles) and 129% (from 1553 to 3561 h), respectively. Furthermore, a prototype pouch cell (506 Wh kg
                    −1
                    ) undergoes 124 cycles. This work establishes an effective strategy that concurrently improves the mechanical and passivation performance of the SEI, tackling the critical challenge of calendar life in Li metal batteries.

title: A Simple Descriptor for Solid‐State Ionic Conductors Across Chemistries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The discovery of new solid‐state ionic conductors remains challenging because ion transport depends sensitively on both mobile‐ion chemistry and the host crystal framework. Although atomistic calculations can evaluate migration barriers directly, simple descriptors can greatly facilitate screening large materials spaces and gaining mechanistic insight. However, existing descriptors often show limited transferability across mobile‐ion chemistries and material classes. Here, we generate a diverse dataset of ion‐migration barriers spanning Li‐, Na‐, K‐, and Mg‐ion conductors across oxides, sulfides, and halides, and use it to systematically benchmark descriptors. From this analysis, we devise distance contraction, ∆
                    d
                    , a simple local geometric descriptor that measures the largest contraction of mobile‐ion–neighbor distances relative to their equilibrium values along a migration pathway. This quantity captures the dominant short‐range repulsion penalty associated with ion migration and consistently distinguishes low‐ from high‐barrier pathways across chemistries. Using ∆
                    d
                    in a high‐throughput screening workflow, we recover many known fast‐ion conductors and identify previously unexplored candidates, with fast‐ion transport validated by nudged elastic band calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Beyond screening, ∆
                    d
                    links diverse ion‐transport mechanisms to a common physical quantity: The largest distance contraction experienced by the migrating ion.

title: Chiral Phonon–Driven Ultrafast Spin Currents in a Non‐Magnetic Ferroelectric
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The discovery that fundamental lattice vibrations can carry angular momentum allows non‐magnetic materials to exhibit properties that until now have only been observable in magnetic materials. However, the role of these specific vibrations, commonly known as chiral phonons, in driving ultrafast spin dynamics has not yet been explored experimentally. Here, using broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the non‐magnetic ferroelectric  generates signals consistent with a ultrafast spin current after excitation with an ultrafast laser pulse, which we attribute to a chiral phonon–induced spin Seebeck effect. We suggest that the transient heating creates an non‐equilibrium phonon distribution, resulting in a net angular momentum and magnetization perpendicular to the thermal gradient, which is converted into a terahertz electromagnetic pulse via an inverse spin‐Hall effect in a thin metal overlayer. The emitted field reverses sign upon flipping the sample orientation or replacing Pt with W, consistent with spin‐current generation. Polarization‐resolved measurements reveal controllable terahertz ellipticity, indicating an additional polarization‐dependent ultrafast response. Our results establish chiral phonons as a route for generating ultrafast spin currents in non‐magnetic materials as well as providing a pathway toward terahertz sources with switchable handedness.

title: Emerging Lipid Nanoparticle Targeting Strategies for Extrahepatic Delivery of RNA Therapeutics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed RNA therapeutics through their high delivery efficiency, scalable manufacturing, and favorable safety profiles, as demonstrated by COVID‐19 mRNA vaccines and clinically approved small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics. However, extending RNA delivery beyond the liver to extrahepatic tissues, including the spleen, lungs, lymph nodes, brain, and tumors, remains challenging because of the intrinsic hepatotropism of conventional LNPs and their limited cell‐type specificity. Recent advances in lipid chemistry, particle engineering, surface functionalization, protein corona modulation, and route‐specific administration have enabled new strategies to redirect LNPs toward specific tissues and cell populations. This review systematically examines these approaches and highlights key determinants of LNP tropism, including formulation composition, surface properties, endogenous protein adsorption, and administration route. We further discuss the clinical translation of extrahepatic LNP delivery, covering clinically validated products, emerging therapeutic candidates, and gaps between preclinical models and human applications. Major challenges include cell‐resolved biodistribution, long‐term safety, repeated‐dose immunogenicity, cross‐study comparability, and standardized quantitative assessment. Finally, we explore how high‐throughput screening, machine learning, and data‐driven design can accelerate the rational optimization of next‐generation LNPs. These advances may facilitate precise tissue‐ and cell‐selective RNA delivery, expanding the therapeutic potential of RNA medicines beyond the liver.

title: Dual Single Atoms Boosting Photocatalytic Upcycling of Raw Polyvinylidene Fluoride Plastic
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents

ABSTRACT

                    1.0

title: Biomimetic Dichalcogenide‐Hybrid Nanozymes With Glutathione Peroxidase‐Like Activity for Liver Protection
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Glutathione peroxidase (GPX)‐mimetic nanozymes are a promising strategy to restore redox homeostasis, but many existing systems rely on metals and remain limited by cytotoxicity, poor selectivity, and susceptibility to catalytic deactivation. Inspired by the active‐site chemistry of native GPX, we designed dichalcogenide‐hybrid mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as inorganic–organic nanozymes with tunable sulfur and selenium environments. Structure–activity analysis showed that GPX‐like performance is governed by chalcogen composition, chalcogen density, and spatial proximity of S/Se within the framework, which together regulate reversible disulfide/diselenide redox cycling and substrate access. Among the materials tested, the diselenide–hybrid framework exhibited the highest activity, with improved selectivity and biocompatibility relative to the disulfide‐hybrid analogue, and conventional metal‐based GPX mimics. Mechanistic studies indicated efficient glutathione‐dependent detoxification of peroxides and lipid peroxides through catalytically active chalcogen intermediates. In vivo, the optimized diselenide‐hybrid material protected against acetaminophen‐induced and rifampicin‐induced liver injury, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored antioxidant capacity, and improved survival. It also alleviated steatosis and metabolic dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) models. These findings establish dichalcogenide–hybrid frameworks as effective GPX‐like nanozymes and a promising platform for the treatment of oxidative stress‐associated liver diseases.

title: Synchronic Multilevel Assembly Toward Mesoporous Nanosized Intercalation‐Type Framework Anodes for Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Intercalation‐type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast‐charging sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation‐type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic‐scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M‐Na
                    4
                    Ti
                    5
                    O
                    12
                    /C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 10 A g
                    −1
                    ) and cycling stability (<0.023% capacity fade per cycle over 1000 cycles at 0.2 A g
                    −1
                    ) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na
                    +
                    diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low‐barrier, nanoscale ion‐conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg
                    −1
                    and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high‐rate battery materials.

title: Robust Sodium–Metal Batteries Through Electrolyte‐Mediated Interfacial Regulation: Fundamentals, Design Strategies, and Operando Characterization
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sodium–metal batteries (SMBs) exhibit high theoretical specific capacity and take advantage of sodium's natural abundance and low cost, showing great promise for broad next‐generation energy‐storage applications. In this review, we summarize the major practical bottlenecks restricting SMB development. The solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) serves as a key mediator to overcome these challenges, and its formation mechanisms are systematically outlined. We comprehensively review diverse electrolyte strategies, including solvent engineering, salt chemistry optimization, additive utilization, high‐concentration, localized high‐concentration, and weakly solvating electrolytes, for modulating Na
                    +
                    transport and generating mechanically robust, ion‐conductive yet electronically insulating SEI layers. We further discuss advanced in‐situ/operando characterizations combined with multiscale computational modeling and machine‐learning techniques as powerful tools to decipher the dynamic evolution of sodium–metal interfaces. Particular focus is placed on the coupled effects of current density, temperature, electrolyte composition, interfacial layers on sodium nucleation, dendrite growth, dead‐sodium formation, and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Finally, future directions for SEI engineering have been outlook toward high‐performance, practical sodium–metal batteries.

title: Healable Thermoset Elastomeric Materials for Passive Radiative Cooling
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology with zero‐energy uptake is an efficient thermal management strategy for the development of sustainable society. Fabrication of PRC materials with intrinsic extensibility/dimensional stability and efficient healability that can adapt to irregular shapes with prolonged lifetime remains a significant challenge. The present study introduces a design principle for mechanically robust and healable PRC films based on a cross‐linked elastomeric network with combined physical interactions and dynamic covalent bonds, which can be readily modulated by inorganic coating and micro‐/nano‐porous hierarchical architectures while retaining extensibility and healability. Such thermosetting elastomeric PRC films are scalable with strong solar reflectance and long‐wave infrared emittance, realizing excellent cooling performance even after physical damage and healing process. It demonstrates excellent roof cooling ability in summer yet efficient ice‐sculpture preservation function in winter. The scalable synthesis of thermoset elastomeric PRC films opens up new pathways to realize flexible, stable and healable PRC materials, highly promising for practical applications.

title: Scientists disrupt less but more persistently with career aging
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Disruption describes the extent to which a scientific work overturns the prior knowledge on which it builds and leads to a new line of research. A scientist’s tendency to produce disruptive work has been found recently to decline over the career. However, the disruption index captures only how strongly a paper overturns prior work and ignores whether that disruption is later accepted or overturned by subsequent research. The persistent disruption (PD) framework adds this second perspective, identifying work that disrupts prior research and is then consolidated rather than displaced by later work. We examine how PD evolves over the career and find the opposite pattern: The probability of producing a persistent disruptive paper increases with career age. Senior scientists disrupt prior work less often compared to young, but once they do, the disruption tends to persist rather than being quickly superseded. Our results suggest that this reversal feature is due to the experience and we corroborate it across several dimensions of recognition. We also show that, at a fixed level of disruptiveness, the more senior the scientist is, it attracts more citations, social-media attention, and research grants. Nobel laureates also show delayed persistent disruptions. They exhibit high disruptive ability early in their careers, yet their prize-winning work appears years later. This lag further indicates that experience is needed to turn disruptive ability into the field’s most celebrated contributions.

title: Geography of groundwater use and depletion in internationally shared aquifers
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Transboundary aquifers (TBAs) underlie 35% of global groundwater-irrigated cropland, yet few are covered by formal cooperative arrangements. Whether this limited cooperation is consequential depends in part on where groundwater is used within shared aquifers, because pumping far from international borders may generate little cross-border impact. Combining
                    
                      
                        ∼
                      
                    
                    116,000 well observations with global irrigation data across all 426 known TBAs, we assess how groundwater use and depletion differ from comparable domestic systems and how they are distributed relative to international borders. While we find no evidence of greater average depletion in TBAs, depletion is more strongly concentrated toward international borders in shared aquifers and varies substantially across systems. Irrigation is also more intensive and concentrated toward borders in shared aquifers, although much of this pattern is attenuated after accounting for border rivers. Groundwater-supplied irrigation remains more border-proximate after accounting for these rivers. A dyad-level typology distinguishes shared systems according to where groundwater demand is concentrated, linking their potential for cross-border interaction to different management options. These findings suggest that transboundary groundwater governance should be organized around the geography of groundwater use and potential cross-border interactions rather than treating shared aquifers as uniform governance units.
