title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts
source: Nature
abstract: The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation1,2,3,4,5, rising tree mortality6,7,8 and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest9,10,11. Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions1,2,3,4,11,12. Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable1,9,13. Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts9,14,15,16,17. Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO2 measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr−1, with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr−1) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011–2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr−1) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019–2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr−1) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr−1) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning.

title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root
source: Nature
abstract: Plant development is highly plastic, with growth and architecture continuously shaped by environmental conditions. Roots, for instance, adjust their development to local water, nutrient and soil conditions. Despite this plasticity, individual root cell types are generally viewed as largely homogeneous populations that progress along a single developmental trajectory1. Here we show that rather than progressing along a single developmental trajectory, most Arabidopsis root cell lineage trajectories exhibit a stereotyped bifid topology, as revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping. One branch is characterized by a transcriptional program that is shared across multiple cell types and enriched for genes associated with environmental responses, including abscisic acid (ABA) signalling. This state occurs reproducibly in a subset of cells across multiple cell types, independent of developmental lineage, thereby revealing an additional layer of root cell identity. It is conserved across Arabidopsis ecotypes and persists despite major perturbations in developmental identity. Moreover, it is reduced in ABA-deficient and ABA-insensitive mutants and becomes more prevalent under water-deficit conditions. Together, these findings reveal an additional layer of root cell identity that is superimposed on developmental lineage and its prevalence is modulated by environmental conditions. These results uncover a previously unrecognized source of environment-associated transcriptional heterogeneity shared across root cell types.

title: CD51 delineates functionally distinct astrocyte subtypes in neural circuits
source: Nature
abstract: Astrocytes perform a diverse range of tasks that facilitate brain physiology, raising the possibility that these diverse astrocytic roles are enabled by functionally distinct subtypes1,2. Recent studies identified molecular diversity among astrocytes3; however, whether this molecular heterogeneity reflects specialized astrocyte subpopulations with distinct functions remains unclear. Here, on the basis of previous molecular and functional studies4, we generated a CD51-FLP mouse line that enables direct comparison of the functional properties between CD51+ and CD51− astrocyte subpopulations in neural circuits in vivo. We show that CD51+ and CD51− astrocytes have unique morphological, physiological and developmental properties in both the cortex and hippocampus. Functional studies demonstrate that CD51+ astrocytes selectively promote synapse formation in the developing cortex and circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Mechanistically, we found that CD51+ astrocytes function through glypican 6 to promote synapse formation in the cortex, while CD51 itself drives circuit plasticity in the hippocampus. Applying these findings to brain injury, we found that CD51+ astrocytes promote functional recovery after stroke through enhanced synaptic remodelling. Taken together, our studies identify specialized astrocyte subpopulations that exhibit distinct functional properties in the developing, mature and injured brain.

title: Multimodal precision diagnostics in clinical xenotransplantation
source: Nature
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in pig-to-human xenotransplantation have successfully prevented hyperacute rejection of kidney, heart, liver and lung xenografts, marking a milestone long considered a critical barrier. However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date. Detection and management of these injuries remain a critical bottleneck, as conventional histopathology and standard clinical monitoring lack the sensitivity required to identify subclinical injury early enough to guide timely intervention. This diagnostic gap underscores an urgent need for the development of advanced, multimodal precision diagnostic frameworks to enhance immune surveillance, which will be essential for standardizing clinical protocols and enabling pathogenesis-driven therapeutic intervention. This approach will inform both immunosuppressive regimens and future gene editing strategies aimed at engineering rejection-resistant porcine organs, ultimately prolonging graft survival. Broad adoption of such an integrative strategy will be essential to transition xenotransplantation from an experimental intervention into a safe, scalable and patient-centred clinical therapy. In this Review, we synthesize recent progress in xenotransplantation and position multimodal precision diagnostics as a pivotal strategy to address the remaining immunological and clinical barriers to widespread clinical implementation.

title: The contribution of salt marshes to wave attenuation during extreme storms
source: Nature
abstract: Salt marshes protect coastlines by attenuating wind waves with their elevated marsh platform and above-ground vegetation1. Confidence in the persistence of this service under a changing climate requires knowledge on how extreme storms damage the platform and vegetation; however, a comprehensive, quantified understanding of salt marsh–wave interactions under extreme events is lacking. A unique experiment was conducted by transferring intact salt marsh to one of the world’s largest wave flumes, and subsequently exposing it to increasingly higher waves that reach up to 2 m significant wave height. We show that marsh substrates can persist with negligible erosion, despite cumulative wave exposure. By contrast, the vegetation was progressively damaged during continued wave exposure, gradually reducing vegetation-related wave attenuation. Results emphasize that vegetation was most effective in attenuating waves at low-energy marsh coasts (up to 1 m), where attenuation exceeded 10% (up to 50%), whereas attenuation at high-energy marsh coasts (wave height > 1 m) does not exceed 10%. Our global assessment supports the differentiation between low- and high-energetic conditions resulting from the flume experiment. Our results suggest that the marsh platform remains stable under extreme wave events and that substantial wave attenuation by marsh vegetation is limited to low-energy marsh coasts.

title: Zeolite-catalysed olefin carbonylation based on tuning spatial confinement
source: Nature
abstract: Carbonylation is an important process used to produce aldehydes, carboxylic acids and esters1,2,3,4,5 that is usually catalysed by homogeneous metal complexes with ligands and iodide promoters6,7,8,9,10,11,12. Koch has reported that protons of mineral acids can also catalyse carbonylation13. Previous studies have demonstrated that Brønsted acidic zeolites can act as a heterogeneous, Koch-type catalyst for carbonylation of alcohols and olefins, but the products in this case are limited to tertiary carboxylic acids14,15,16,17,18. Here we show that targeted use of spatial confinement in a zeolite together with a high CO/olefin ratio can help break this limitation. We report that, with FER zeolite and a CO/olefin ratio of 360, olefin carbonylation can produce primary and secondary carboxylic acids as the main products; ethylene carbonylation to propanoic acid (PA) is achieved with 80% selectivity over 100 h and propylene carbonylation to isobutyric acid (IBA) is achieved with 95% selectivity over 750 h. The propylene and ethylene carbonylation selectivities decrease to 61% and 57%, respectively, as the CO/olefin ratio decreases to 24 and 90, respectively. Experiments in combination with theoretical calculations suggest that T2-O5 in eight-membered ring (8-MR) cavities of FER zeolite are the primary active sites for ethylene carbonylation and T3-O1 in ten-membered rings (10-MRs) are the primary active sites for propylene carbonylation. Our findings open new directions for olefin carbonylation and provide critical insights into the prerequisites for developing new zeolite-based carbonylation processes.

title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis
source: Nature
abstract: Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species1,2,3, yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans. Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2–BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington’s disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

title: Concentration‑dependent switching between ligand‑like and solvent‑like lipid regulation in a model ion channel
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

title: A single archaeon couples long-chain fatty acid oxidation to methanogenesis
source: Nature
abstract: Anaerobic degradation of complex organic compounds to methane and carbon dioxide is common in the deep subsurface biosphere and has long been considered to require syntrophic cooperation, with methanogens confined to the terminal use of simple C1 and C2 substrates. Thermodynamic considerations, multi-omics analyses and microcosm experiments suggest that archaeal lineages are capable of methanogenic degradation of complex substrates1,2,3,4,5,6. However, experimental validation in pure culture was lacking. Here we report the isolation of a thermophilic archaeon, Methanoglobus dolicholipophagus AA-75, affiliated with Archaeoglobi, from a Chinese petroleum reservoir. Strain AA-75 not only converts methanol into methane, carbon dioxide and acetate, but also uses saturated fatty acids varying from C7:0 to C18:0 and unsaturated fatty acids including C16:1, C18:1 and C18:2 to produce methane. We term the latter lipotrophic methanogenesis, which integrates β-oxidation of fatty acids with the Wood–Ljungdahl pathway and the canonical methyl-tetrahydromethanopterin:coenzyme M methyltransferase and methyl-coenzyme M reductase complexes, together with an intracellular electron transfer system. A formaldehyde-methanol branch probably functions as an auxiliary route for C1 metabolism during methanogenesis. Methane produced from stearate is moderately 13C-enriched (δ13C–CH4 = −40.0‰ to −36.3‰), distinct from the strong 13C depletion characteristic of canonical methanogenic pathways. These findings demonstrate that methanogens can function as primary degraders of complex organic matter, challenging the classical syntrophic paradigm and calling for refinement of current models of carbon cycling in the deep subsurface biosphere.

title: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts
source: Nature
abstract: The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins.1–5 This challenge is acute for metal polypyridine photocatalysts, which are widely used in visible-light chemistry but have not enabled highly enantioselective photocatalysis within protein scaffolds. In this study, we show that generative protein design6–8 can create de novo scaffolds that selectively bind these photocatalysts and that directed evolution converts the resulting artificial metalloenzymes into efficient, highly enantioselective photocatalysts9. The evolved proteins support diverse light-driven reactions, high catalyst turnover and catalyst recycling, and can function with commercially available racemic metal complexes. Spectroscopic studies show that the protein environment extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity. These findings establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds for synthetic metal complexes that lack natural protein partners and provide a strategy for combining protein design and evolution to control non-natural catalytic chemistry.

This work establishes ligand engineering as a general strategy to tune excited-state dynamics in metal nanoclusters, offering chemists a new materials design route for next-generation optoelectronics beyond conventional semiconductors.

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) has established a new approach for narrowband blue organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs), yet effectively suppressing intermolecular interactions especially at high doping concentrations while preserving the intrinsic narrowband emission remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel designing paradigm is proposed for achieving anti‐quenching narrowband emission in MR‐TADF molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1‐b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. The proof‐of‐concept emitter
                    DT‐BON1

As a result, the emission peaks and full width at half maximum show virtually no variation with changing doping concentration from 1 wt% to 20 wt%. Moreover, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% even at 20 wt% doping concentration endowed by the outstanding anti‐quenching characteristics. The

ABSTRACT
                  
                    Planar tetracoordinate halides have been widely explored by quantum computational approaches but remain rare as deliberately targeted experimental motifs. Here we show that these geometries can be accessed by supramolecular enforcement, and challenge its connection to the VSEPR model. Bowl‐shaped calix[4]pyrrolato indium units preorganize four lithium ions into a confined Li

The experimental series shows that halide planarity is highly sensitive to subtle supramolecular effects, such as calix[4]pyrrolato doming and crystal packing, experimentally confirming the generally low angular deformation energies. The results establish supramolecular enforcement as a rational design principle for planar tetracoordinate heavier halides and show that such motifs are accessible outcomes of engineered electrostatic cavities.

abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The single crystal cathodes show significant superiority in cycling stability and safety, but are restricted by high costs, as current preparation strategies often lead to particle agglomeration. Here, we develop a new strategy of surface high‐valence metal doping to prepare the highly dispersed single crystal LiNi
                    0.90
                    Mn

                    Co

                    (SC‐NCM90) in low‐cost. The surface substitution of Ni
                    2+/3+
                    by W
                    6+
                    /Mo
                    6+
                    facilitates to enhancing the bond with O, suppressing cation interdiffusion, benefiting particle dispersion, and high voltage stability. The surface Mo‐doping lowers the energy of (104) plane and stimulates its prior growth, favoring fast Li

title: Electric Double Layer‐Driven Surface Reconstruction Enables Cooperative Zn(002)/(101) Growth for High‐Utilization Zinc Anodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous zinc batteries are limited by the mismatch between dynamic interfacial chemistry and anisotropic Zn crystallization. Here, imidazolidinyl urea (IDU) is used to couple electric double layer (EDL) reconstruction with Zn surface reorganization. IDU preferentially enriches at the Zn/electrolyte interface, displaces interfacial water, and interacts strongly with Zn(100). In situ spectroscopic ellipsometry, quartz crystal microbalance, and neutron reflectivity reveal transient removal and reconstruction of surface Zn rather than simple molecular adsorption. The reconstructed interface suppresses Zn(100) and promotes cooperative Zn(002)/(101) evolution, enabling compact deposition with favorable kinetics. Meanwhile, the water‐deficient EDL and hybrid organic‐inorganic interphase inhibit parasitic reactions and stabilize the interfacial environment. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells cycle for over 6000 h at 4 mA cm
                    −2
                    and 2 mAh cm
                    −2
                    , while Zn||Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.81% over 3000 cycles. Stable operation is further maintained at −10°C and under high Zn utilization. Zn||CVO full cells retain 75% capacity after 650 cycles at an N/P ratio of 2.9, and a 21 mAh pouch cell preserves 84% capacity after 400 cycles. This work links EDL reconstruction with crystallographic evolution to enable highly reversible and practically relevant Zn metal anodes.

title: Dual Anion‐Involved Interfacial Chemistry Enables Ultra‐Stable PEO‐Based Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries by Suppressing NMP‐Induced Side Reactions
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The incorporation of solvent N‐methylpyrrolidone (NMP) into polyethylene oxide (PEO) weakens EO‐Li
                    +
                    interaction and boosts Li
                    +
                    transport via strong Li
                    +
                    affinity, but free NMP inevitably reacts with Li metal, undermining interface stability. Herein, we report a dual‐anion coordination strategy that repurposes the residual NMP from a “side‐reaction source” into a “functional component”. LiDFOB and LiNO
                    3
                    are introduced as dual‐salt additives into an NMP‐containing PEO/LiTFSI system. Leveraging the preferential coordination of DFOB– and NO
                    3
                    –
                    with Li
                    +
                    , an anion‐enriched solvation sheath is constructed, which strengthens the Li
                    +
                    ‐NMP interactions. The modified coordination environment facilitates the preferential formation of a kinetically stable, anion‐derived solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively mitigating interfacial side reactions between the NMP and Li metal. As a result, the obtained electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.69 × 10
                    −4
                    S cm
                    −1
                    and stable cycling over 1200 h at room temperature. The assembled Li/LFP cell exhibits a high capacity retention of 93% after 2000 cycles. Even at room temperate and 0°C, the assembled Li/LFP cell maintains stable and efficient cycling. This work establishes a universal solvent structure tailoring strategy to regulate reactive solvent molecules, opening a fresh avenue for high‐performance PEO‐based solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Synergistic Proton Transport Regulation and Interfacial Anion Adsorption Engineering in ZIF‐8‐Derived PtCu Electrocatalysts for High‐Performance Light and Heavy‐Duty PEM Fuel Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Engineering catalyst‐ionomer interfaces is critical for overcoming the coupled kinetic and transport limitations that impede the commercialization of low‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (LT‐PEMFCs). Herein, a PtCu alloy supported on a zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8‐derived 3D‐hierarchical carbon framework is developed to simultaneously regulate proton transport and interfacial anion adsorption within the catalyst layer. Oxophilic Cu preferentially interacts with Nafion's sulfonate groups, mitigating excessive adsorption on Pt, while the 3D‐hierarchical porous architecture promotes homogeneous ionomer distribution, continuous proton‐conduction pathways, and efficient water transport. Hydrogen underpotential deposition (HUPD) half‐cell analysis across various concentrations of Nafion revealed Temkin‐type adsorption features and demonstrated weakened Nafion adsorption following Cu incorporation, supported by various physical and theoretical analyses. The optimized catalyst exhibits a reduced Tafel slope of 55.8 mV dec
                    −
                    1
                    , delivering 0.75 A mg
                    Pt
                    −1
                    at 0.90 V
                    IR‐free
                    under H
                    2
                    ‐O
                    2
                    operation, exceeding the U.S. DOE target. Membrane electrode assemblies achieved 1.52 and 1.80 A cm
                    −
                    2
                    at 0.70 V under light‐ and heavy‐duty conditions after 30k accelerated stress‐test cycles. Sequential Distribution of Relaxation Time impedance analysis further demonstrates that synergistic regulation of catalyst‐ionomer interactions and proton transport simultaneously mitigates kinetic, ohmic, and mass‐transport losses, providing a general design strategy for high‐performance LT‐PEMFC.

title: An Ultrathin Ionic COF Self‐Supporting Proton Exchange Membrane Through Stacking of Few‐Layer Nanosheets Grown From High‐Curvature Micro‐Interface for Fuel Cell
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Ultrathin self‐supporting ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) proton exchange membranes (PEM) are crucial for low‐resistance sustainable energy applications but remain challenging to fabricate. The key to fabricating ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF membranes lies in the compact stacking of iCOF nanosheets, which remains inaccessible through micro‐interfacial polymerization systems. Herein, we report for the first time an ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM constructed by growing few‐layer iCOF nanosheets at high‐curvature micro‐interfaces, alongside a proposed growth mechanism. The curved iCOF exhibits reduced interlayer attraction due to a twisted configuration, and enhanced solvation‐driven exfoliation arising from greater exposure of sulfonic acid groups to water. It avoids the commonly reported nanosphere‐like morphologies in previously reported micro‐interfacial assembly systems by regulating the oil‐in‐water microemulsion interface using weakly surface‐active octanoic acid, which effectively balances between the confined oil phase growth and the unconfined aqueous phase exfoliation. As‐prepared iCOF few‐layer nanosheets (1.3–1.5 nm) expose abundant reactive terminal groups for interlayer crosslinking under the vacuum filtration pressure gradient, leading to ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM (3.2–15.1 µm) with compact layer stacking, good mechanical robustness, and excellent scalability (20 cm in diameter). A fuel cell peak power density of 2017.7 mW cm
                    −2
                    at 80°C is achieved, surpassing recently reported iCOF‐based membranes.

title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

title: Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization–selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.

title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4+ T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4
                    +
                    responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4
                    +
                    response was strongly T helper 1 (T
                    H
                    1)–polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor–α and minimal T
                    H
                    2 cytokines. Both CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F–specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

title: Physical confinement modulates the rate-limiting transition in the release of phosphate from actin filaments
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The nucleotide state and rates of transitions between states regulate the dynamics of ATPases. Slow inorganic phosphate (P
                    i
                    ) release following ATP hydrolysis is often rate limiting and associated with key conformational changes. Actin filaments offer a unique opportunity to understand the fundamentals of P
                    i
                    release because identical subunits at filament ends and the interior release P
                    i
                    at markedly different rates. The molecular origin of this difference is debated, so we used extensive all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize P
                    i
                    release from different subunits within an actin filament. The calculated dissociation rates of P
                    i
                    from ADP-Mg
                    2+
                    in the active site correlate with experimentally measured P
                    i
                    release rates and scale inversely with the numbers of water molecules in the cavity surrounding the γ-phosphate. Simulations show that egress of P
                    i
                    through the protein channels, including through the N111-R177 backdoor, is not rate limiting and that subunits at the filament ends use alternative egress pathways.

title: Spatial decoupling of recognition and signaling in aptamer switches via tri-strand intermolecular competition
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Despite decades of progress in aptamer engineering, the development of a single, modular signaling architecture capable of transducing target recognition into a measurable output across structurally diverse analytes remains an unmet challenge in biosensing. We report the Competitor Bridge Aptamer (CoBrA) framework: a modular DNA tridomain architecture that functionally isolates target recognition from signal transduction. Unlike conventional sensors where signal output depends on unpredictable aptamer folding, the CoBrA system uses an aptamer switch to trigger a predictable, concerted spatial displacement between signaling end points. By leveraging computational simulations and energetic balancing, we systematically optimized the CoBrA framework to consolidate recognition, displacement, and ratiometric signaling within a single, minimal-component system. Using the dopamine and cortisol aptamers as models, we demonstrate strong thermodynamic and kinetic synchronization between the Cy3 and Cy5 channels across both targets for dopamine (Cy3:
                    K
                    d
                     = 13.3 ± 3.2 μM, τ = 447 ± 31 seconds; Cy5:
                    K
                    d
                     = 24.0 ± 3.3 μM, τ = 537 ± 22 seconds) and cortisol (Cy3:
                    K
                    d
                     = 36.6 ± 3.9 μM, τ = 205 ± 7 seconds; Cy5:
                    K
                    d
                     = 30.7 ± 5.5 μM, τ = 259 ± 4 seconds) in buffer, serum, and artificial cerebrospinal fluid. Because the signaling event is a predictable, geometry-defined change rather than a fluorescence-specific phenomenon, this architecture is in principle adaptable to surface-based transduction modalities, including electrochemical, field-effect transistor, and plasmonic readouts.

title: High ambipolar mobility fluorinated MXene for ultrasensitive biosensing transistors
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) are emerging as transformative materials for bioelectronics. However, the advancement of MXene-based field-effect transistor (FET) biosensors is hindered by the lack of high-quality aqueous-stable materials and the low signal transduction efficiency intrinsic to their metallic nature. To address these issues, we report an ultrasensitive biosensing platform enabled by an in-situ fluorination strategy of MXene. By substituting unstable oxygen-containing terminations with chemically stable fluorine terminations in a mild reaction, we synthesized high-quality fluorinated MXene with the record-breaking ambipolar field-effect mobility (μ
                    p
                     = 10.42 cm
                    2
                     V
                    −1
                     s
                    −1
                    , μ
                    n

                    2
                     V
                    −1
                     s
                    −1
                    ). The highly electronegative fluorinated interface suppresses interfacial electrical double-layer capacitance, boosting signal transduction efficiency. Consequently, the platform achieves the lowest limit of detection (LOD) of 0.26 fg ml
                    −1

                    Mycobacterium tuberculosis

Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

title: Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices—ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors—have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe
                    2
                    /LiAl
                    2
                    Fe
                    3
                    O
                    8
                    (LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe
                    2
                    /LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe
                    2
                    . The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field–temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe
                    2
                    . Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.

title: Translational control of microglial metabolism, inflammatory responses, and survival by the eIF4E-binding proteins
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In Alzheimer’s disease (AD), activation of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway promotes microglial neuroprotective functions by engaging multiple cell receptors. However, the relevant downstream effectors are not fully understood. mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) promotes mRNA translation by phosphorylating and inactivating eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E-binding protein 1 and 2 (4E-BP1/2), which are expressed in microglia. 4E-BP1 levels in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) are elevated in AD and correlate with markers of microglial reactivity and disease progression. Using linear regression analysis, we found that elevated CSF 4E-BP1 levels strengthen the association between soluble TREM2 levels and neurodegeneration in amyloid-positive individuals. To investigate the underlying mechanism, we performed in vitro experiments demonstrating that amyloid-β inactivated 4E-BP1 in murine microglia. The mTOR-mediated inactivation is highly dependent on Spleen Tyrosine Kinase (SYK) signaling and repeated exposure to amyloid-β impaired this process, whereas prolonged exposure increased 4E-BP1 levels in microglia. Deletion of 4E-BP1/2 resulted in increased mitochondrial mass and oxidative phosphorylation, reduced pro-inflammatory signaling, and protected microglia from amyloid-induced apoptosis. Thus, impaired 4E-BP1 inactivation—due to reduced mTOR signaling or excess 4E-BP1—disrupts immune resolution, leading to metabolic exhaustion and microglial cell death. We identify the SYK–mTORC1–4E-BP1 signaling axis as a key regulator of microglial mitochondrial biogenesis and immune resolution in AD.

title: Naturalistic spatial education engages distinct neural processes for mental rotation, cognitive load, and linguistic demands
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Neuroscience studies typically isolate spatial cognition using simplified tasks targeting a single cognitive process. However, during formal spatial education, the brain rarely performs one cognitive operation at a time. Here, we used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to assess neural systems involved in dynamically processing an educational spatial visualization lesson. We quantified lesson content using an instructional-design framework capturing variation in spatial complexity, cognitive load, and verbal density. We then characterized how instructional demands modulated brain function using content-evoked responses, functional connectivity, and network-centrality. Spatial transformations during instruction robustly recruited parietal and premotor regions, which were linearly modulated by spatial complexity. This parietal dominance aligns with theories that these areas encode geometric and quantitative dimensions. In contrast, domain-general frontal activity tracked overall processing demands, and language regions tracked verbal density. Activity also varied with learners’ spatial abilities: higher spatial performers showed stronger modulation of parietal and premotor regions as spatial demands increased, and greater domain-general modulation across content types. Thus, the same circuitry representing spatial transformations during instruction also reflects individual variation in spatial cognition. Parietal regions showed the highest centrality and strongest within-network coherence, marking them as the central hub of the system, and distinguishing them from less central and less coherent domain-general regions. Together, the findings reveal how the brain dynamically decomposes complex spatial instruction, preserving parietal-centered spatial processing, while coordinating support from premotor, domain-general, and language systems. These findings begin to reveal how spatial cognition operates within the complexity of formal instruction.

title: Random, fragile, or correlated: Mechanisms of synteny decay in mammals
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: We formalize three models of genome evolution, yielding analytical distributions of synteny block sizes between pairs of genomes. To evaluate each model, we fit theoretical synteny block size distributions to empirical distributions from a comparative analysis of nearly 200 mammalian genomes. Between the random breakage model (RBM), with uniformly distributed breakpoints, the fragile breakage model (FBM) with breakpoint hotspots, and what we term the correlated breakage model (CBM) with pairs of nearby breakpoints, we find that the FBM and CBM are far more consistent with mammalian genome evolution than the RBM. Inferred parameters of each model qualitatively agree with previously calculated rates of mammalian genome evolution. The FBM and CBM perform comparably with each other, suggesting that either model could serve as an improved null model of genome evolution to use in statistical tests for syntenic regions that are unlikely to exist due to random chance.

title: IL36γ signaling promotes mammalian anti-tick immunity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Ticks, like
                    Ixodes scapularis
                    , can parasitize a diverse array of vertebrates, favoring natural hosts but feeding opportunistically on others. Natural hosts, as well as permissive hosts such as laboratory mice, tolerate repeated infestations, while many incidental hosts may acquire anti-tick immunity, as first described in guinea pigs. We show that tick-immune guinea pigs display altered dermal cytology and a distinct transcriptome, predominantly upregulating the IL36γ cytokine. Interference with IL36γ signaling, via gene knockdown, chemical inhibition, or its natural antagonist IL36RN, reversed anti-tick immunity in guinea pigs. Conversely, genome engineering to silence IL36RN in C3H mice, representing a permissive host, disrupted tick engorgement, interfering with the transmission of Lyme disease pathogens. These findings firmly establish IL36γ as a central mediator of protective anti-tick immunity involving
                    I. scapularis
                    in mammalian hosts and support future strategies to interfere with tick-transmitted infections.

title: Enhancing simulations of disordered protein ensembles with chemical shift restraints in coarse-grained models
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
With more than one third of the human proteome being structurally disordered, intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are key contributors to complex cellular functions, despite their highly dynamic conformational ensembles remaining elusive to conventional techniques in structural biology. Coarse-grained (CG) simulation methods thus serve as a gold standard to refine IDP ensembles. These methods, when relying on elastic network models or rigid body to sample secondary structure, are however inherently limited in their capability to model and sample transient secondary structure at a residue-level resolution as informed by experimental data. This fundamental limitation persists despite experimental evidence suggesting that transient structural propensities are a fundamental hallmark of IDP function. Through an artificial neural network capable of predicting backbone chemical shifts from C
                    α
                    -only protein conformations, we present a generalized framework which does not rely on dihedral parameterization to equip one bead-per-aminoacid CG force fields with the ability to sample functional elements of secondary structure. When applied on a large set of IDPs in isolation or condensates, our approach correctly recapitulates both local and global arrangements, yielding experimentally informed ensembles that can inform structure-mediated function and resolve force field limitations. This can yield a fruitful exploration of ensemble-to-function relationships in IDPs, allowing to explore phenomena such as secondary structure propensity and nucleation in condensates, conformationally selected binding motifs across disordered ensembles or conformational preferences of sequence-specific short-linear motifs.

title: Macromolecular association creates dispersity of components that determines liquid–liquid phase separation of oppositely charged polyions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Developing insight into liquid–liquid phase separation in complex polyelectrolyte mixtures has acquired new urgency considering the role this process plays in the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are involved in diverse processes including, stress response, signal transduction, metabolism, gene regulation, and many human diseases. Condensates can be viewed as a biological membraneless structure situated, in scale and function, between macromolecules and cells. The physical properties of, and the physico-chemical environments within, condensates are very important determinants of their biological function. These properties and environments are determined by the phase separation process. Earlier experimental work in one of our laboratories characterized in detail a phase separation process in solutions of oppositely charged polypeptides. Considering new information being developed on macromolecular association in homogeneous solutions of oppositely charged polyions, we have revisited our earlier data looking into the influence of intermolecular association on the outcome of the phase transition. Such influence is clearly established in this Brief Report. We demonstrate that dispersity of species in homogeneous solution owing to macromolecular association affects phase separation by creating an open miscibility gap, leading to a dependence of the phase compositions on the initial polymer volume fraction. It is very likely that this plays a significant role in the formation of condensates in the biological context that may have been overlooked.

title: Molecular fossils of an ancestral code revealed by large-scale analysis of tRNAs
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Modern tRNAs are thought to have evolved from simpler RNA minihelices resembling acceptor stems, some of which could be specifically aminoacylated. A central and testable prediction of minihelix-based models is that vestiges of ancestral coding relationships should remain embedded within the acceptor stems of contemporary tRNAs and should persist after correction for structural constraints. Here, we ask whether cognate anticodon-like triplets are statistically enriched in nonanticodon regions of modern tRNAs beyond what would be expected from structural and compositional constraints alone. Using a curated dataset of 77,335 canonical tRNA sequences and a structure-aware statistical framework, we find that for a subset of amino acids cognate anticodon-like triplets are significantly enriched in acceptor stems and, to a lesser extent, in other structural domains. Notably, these amino acids include those previously shown to support specific minihelix aminoacylation [Y. M. Hou, P. Schimmel,
                    Nature
                    333
                    , 140–145 (1988); C. Francklyn, P. Schimmel,
                    Nature
                    337
                    , 478–481 (1989)]. The strongest acceptor-stem signals survive structure-preserving null models, and cluster nonrandomly against proposed chronologies of amino acid incorporation into the genetic code. Together, these findings identify molecular fossils within modern tRNAs consistent with the persistence of an ancestral operational code, and provide refined statistical support for the notion that extant codon–amino acid relationships evolved from early aminoacylation systems involving RNA minihelices.

title: Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N2O5 hydrolysis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N
                    2
                    O
                    5
                    hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.

title: Comparative analysis of photocatalytic, enzymatic, and chemical approaches to identify canonical and noncanonical surfaceomes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: The cell surface is a critical nexus in cellular communication and a rich landscape yielding the majority of current therapeutic targets, yet only a small fraction of cell surface proteins have been targeted therapeutically. The cell surface proteome (surfaceome) comprises only ~1% of the human proteome by mass, motivating enrichment strategies to detect surfaceome alterations in disease for drug target discovery. Developments in photocatalytic technology have revolutionized the study of protein neighborhoods around specific targets of interest, but photocatalysis has been underutilized for global surfaceome analysis. Here, we describe five distinct photocatalytic surfaceomics strategies, all without the need for cellular engineering, that apply the photocatalyst Eosin Y attached to different cell surface structures: direct glycan ligation, glycan attachment via two different lectins, membrane insertion, and free in extracellular space. We systematically compare these photocatalytic surfaceomics methods to each other as well as to three established chemical and enzymatic surfaceomics methods. We demonstrate that the different photocatalytic surfaceomics techniques achieve broadly similar canonical cell surface protein enrichment but show some important differences reflective of cell surface attachment mechanism. These mechanistically orthogonal surfaceomics techniques consistently identified numerous nonglycosylated proteins with high concordance, many of which represent an underappreciated class of noncanonical cell surface proteins lacking traditional cell surface protein features that may represent potential drug targets. This study substantially expands options for surfaceomics methods using photocatalytic proximity labeling.

title: Structure of a sparsely populated chimeric intermediate that facilitates fold-switching of a metamorphic protein
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Metamorphic proteins challenge the single-sequence-structure-function paradigm by switching between distinct folds that often adopt complementary functions. However, the conformational states sampled along the fold-switching pathway have remained elusive because they are transient and unstable. Using multinuclear chemical exchange saturation transfer and relaxation dispersion NMR, combined with chemical shift–based structure determination and protein engineering, we visualized the atomic resolution structure of an “invisible” state of the metamorphic chemokine lymphotactin. This state is a chimera that integrates the secondary and tertiary structure of one fold with the quaternary assembly of the other. Locking lymphotactin into a single conformation abolishes access to this state, supporting its role as an on-pathway intermediate in metamorphosis. The stabilization of such hybrid intermediates is likely to have facilitated the evolution of fold-switching and represents a powerful strategy for protein design.

title: Linguistic intervention unlocks the economic gains of diversity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Gains from trade generate prosperity, yet interpersonal exchange can falter along racial lines. We study incentivized experimental economies where participants must spontaneously initiate and sustain trading relationships with others whose race is visible. When the highest gains from trade require cross-race exchange, diverse economies underperform: welfare and specialization suffer as many retreat to autarky. This underperformance reflects not segregation into racial trading blocs, but a collapse in exchange. Opportunities for contact alone do not close the performance gap, which persists and even widens over time. To understand why, we turn to communication itself. Lower welfare is associated with less communication, fewer expressions of affiliation and achievement, and less explicit signaling of needs, deficits, and surpluses. We call this communicative misalignment: differences in shared-language use that raise search, bargaining, and coordination costs. A brief linguistic intervention equips participants with a communicative toolkit. It increases communication volume and the frequency of motivational and state-signaling language. Crucially, when gains depend on cross-race exchange, the intervention restores specialization and cross-race trade, closing the performance gap. Its effects are minimal when efficient trade need not cross race, indicating specificity rather than generic skill training. Language thus operates bidirectionally, both revealing the state of cooperation and causally shaping it. Although we examine racial boundaries, the mechanism may operate along other fault lines where interactional norms diverge, including hierarchy, geography, or culture. Language, a primary conduit of culture, can impede exchange when misaligned and facilitate it when aligned. This suggests a scalable micro-governance tool for reducing transaction costs.

title: C1ql2 gates stress vulnerability by regulating microglia-mediated synaptic pruning in the BLA-vHPC circuit
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Synaptic remodeling in emotional circuits contributes to the development of stress-related emotional disorders. However, such remodeling generally exhibits considerable heterogeneity across specific neuronal populations and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identified
                    C1ql2
                    as a key molecular regulator that governs projection-specific synaptic vulnerability within basolateral amygdala (BLA). Transcriptional profiling revealed that
                    C1ql2
                    expression is enriched in BLA neurons projecting to ventral hippocampus (BLA
                    →vHPC
                    PNs), but not in those projecting to nucleus accumbens (NAc), and is significantly down-regulated following chronic social defeat stress (CSDS). Gain- and loss-of-function manipulations demonstrated that
                    C1ql2
                    regulates stress-induced neuronal remodeling in BLA
                    →vHPC
                    PNs, including dendritic hypertrophy, synaptic outgrowth, and enhanced glutamatergic transmission, thereby shaping susceptibility to anxiety-like behavior. We further found that CSDS-induced
                    C1ql2
                    loss impairs microglial engulfment of BLA
                    →vHPC
                    PNs synapses, leading to aberrant synaptic accumulation. Our findings establish C1ql2-mediated neuron-microglia cross talk that critically regulates circuit-specific synaptic pathophysiology in stress-related disorders.

title: Gene conversion is a key driver of diversity hotspots in Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens and virulence-associated loci
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Despite the long-held view of
                    Mycobacterium tuberculosis
                    (
                    Mtb
                    ) as a genetically conserved pathogen, many genomic regions remain poorly resolved due to high sequence homology and repetitive content. Using complete genome assemblies generated from long-read sequencing of 151 globally representative clinical isolates, we comprehensively analyzed genome-wide patterns of genetic diversity and evolution across the
                    Mtb
                    genome. Our analysis uncovers pronounced diversity hotspots within paralogous regions (PRs) generated by recurrent gene conversion between homologous genes. In many cases, these hotspots exhibit more than an order of magnitude greater genetic diversity than the rest of the
                    Mtb
                    genome, which is otherwise characterized by remarkably low variation. Mutations within these regions display clustered substitution patterns, excess paralog-matching variants, and distinct mutational spectra consistent with ongoing gene conversion. Our analysis identifies over 300 individual gene conversion events (GCEs) distributed throughout the
                    Mtb
                    phylogeny. These GCEs occur predominantly within gene families associated with virulence and host–pathogen interactions, including the PE, PPE, and ESX families. Several of the most pronounced diversity hotspots occur in antigens encoded within PRs. Among these, the vaccine candidate PPE18 harbors mutations in validated epitope sequences and predicted alterations in HLA-II binding. Together, these findings demonstrate that gene conversion actively shapes antigenic and virulence-associated diversity in
                    Mtb
                    .

title: Validation of targets linked to weight gain in C57BL/6 mice and translational aspects in humans
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Obesity is linked to complex interactions between an organism’s genetic background and its environment. Mouse models have been invaluable research tools to study obesity, with C57BL/6N being widely studied, given its propensity for weight gain on a high-fat diet (HFD). Despite this, the genetic basis of its susceptibility is poorly understood. In a partner paper we have identified SNP variants in 11 genes causing susceptibility to, or protection against, HFD-induced obesity in male C57BL/6N mice explaining 87% of the individual variation in fat gain. Surprisingly, most of them were maximally expressed outside the brain. In this study, we further validate some of these targets. We demonstrate that tissue-specific inhibition of Nova1 and Mchr1 in muscle, Nr1i3 in liver, and Ahr in lung and liver led to resistance to HFD–induced obesity or glucose intolerance. Further RNAseq analysis revealed that mTOR, Acox1, IL-15, and eIF2a signals are positioned downstream of these genes, potentially mediating their effects on obesity susceptibility. Importantly, variants in eight of the genes identified here have been previously implicated in human obesity, suggesting that a deeper understanding of the genetic/environment interactions of model systems can inform this complex human disease. Our work confirms that body fat regulation is likely more complex than current models which focus on the brain–adipose axis suggest.

title: Harry L. Swinney: Nonlinear science and chaos pioneer
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Harry Leonard Swinney passed away peacefully at his home in Austin, Texas, on July 13, 2026, at the age of 87. Harry was an exceptional experimental physicist, well-known for elegant studies of instabilities, nonlinear dynamics, chaos and pattern formation in a wide variety of fluid, chemical, and granular systems, work whose influence propagated into numerous scientific and engineering disciplines well beyond the particular problems that prompted it. The late Russell Donnelly of the University of Oregon used to say, “Harry is a prince”; Russ meant it, in the spirit of the tenth-century Persian poet Ferdowsi, as a compliment affirming the nobility, dignity, integrity, and grace with which Harry pursued his science and treated everyone he worked alongside.

title: Signal peptides for engineered protein secretion by free and hydrogel-encapsulated cyanobacteria
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Cyanobacteria provide a promising platform for light-driven heterologous protein production. In heterologous production systems, cells are typically lysed for product purification or to facilitate interaction with external substrates, unless the product is secreted. Fusion to molecular “shipping labels” known as signal peptides can target chimeric proteins to native membrane translocation pathways and result in secretion. In this work, we identified signal peptides from the model cyanobacterium
                    Synechococcus elongatus
                    PCC 7942 (
                    S. elongatus
                    ) and genetically fused to two heterologous enzymes: the reporter nanoluciferase (NLuc) and an oxidative laccase (CotA). Increased extracellular activity was observed for one or more signal-protein variants for both enzymes. Furthermore, cells of
                    S. elongatus
                    producing a signal-laccase chimera were encapsulated within an alginate hydrogel, and the resulting engineered living material released sufficient enzyme to decolorize a dye pollutant in its surroundings. These findings streamline recombinant protein production in cyanobacteria and facilitate environmental interactions with cell products, expanding the potential applications of both free-living and material-encapsulated cyanobacteria.

title: In-cloud motions shape warm-rain production in marine clouds: Evidence from multiyear observations
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Despite years of research, the processes controlling warm-rain formation remain uncertain. Leveraging multiple years of observations collected across four oceanic regions, we systematically reassess the properties of precipitation just beneath cloud base. The observations show that warm-rain characteristics are remarkably consistent within cloud regimes yet differ substantially between stratocumulus and cumulus, indicating that cloud-regime properties exert a stronger influence on warm precipitation than regional environmental variability. Precipitation is observed beneath marine stratocumulus in over 56% of cloudy columns with liquid water path (LWP) <130 g m
                    −2
                    , rising to more than 84% in columns with LWP beyond 130 g m
                    −2
                    . This indicates that marine stratocumulus routinely support warm-rain formation and suggests that barriers to precipitation onset in this regime are weaker than commonly assumed. For the same LWP, oceanic cumulus precipitate less frequently than stratocumulus but on average produce two times larger and one to two orders of magnitude fewer precipitation drops. This contrast is consistent with cumulus presenting two times stronger updrafts and lower adiabaticity than stratocumulus, both of which can affect drop growth histories. Whereas the precipitation characteristics of stratocumulus are generally consistent with growth by collision–coalescence during gravitational free fall in low LWP clouds, those of cumulus cannot be explained without invoking additional processes. Together, these findings suggest that warm-precipitation parameterizations should more explicitly account for the influence of small-scale dynamical processes on precipitation growth. The apparent importance of drop growth histories further motivates continued exploration of Lagrangian particle-tracking approaches in both models and observations.

title: Mass-independent oxygen isotope fractionation driven by energetic-particle irradiation of icy solids
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Mass-independent isotope fractionation (MIF) of oxygen provides key insights into atmospheric chemistry and the origin of isotopic anomalies in planetary materials. To date, MIF has been primarily associated with gas-phase processes involving symmetry-dependent reaction pathways, most notably ozone formation. Whether analogous effects can arise in condensed phases or at interfaces remains an open question. Here we report laboratory experiments demonstrating that energetic particle irradiation of icy oxide surfaces produces mass-independent oxygen isotope fractionation at temperatures as low as 10 K. Electron irradiation of SiO
                    2
                    and Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    substrates in the presence of H
                    2
                    O ice results in measurable shifts in Δ
                    17
                    O in the underlying solids. The resulting three-isotope relationships include slope-1-like behavior in SiO
                    2
                    and Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    and distinct, substrate-dependent trends in Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    , indicating that irradiation-induced defect formation and interfacial chemistry govern the isotope effects. The magnitude of the observed anomalies demonstrates that irradiation-driven processes can generate substantial oxygen isotope heterogeneity in condensed phases. These results identify a previously unrecognized class of MIF and provide a quantitative framework for interpreting oxygen isotope signatures in radiation-processed environments, including interstellar grains and early solar system materials.

title: CD28 costimulation is organized by signaling condensates and counteracted by PD-1
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: T cell activation relies on the coordinated integration of T cell receptor (TCR) and cosignaling pathways, yet how these signals are physically organized remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that CD28 co-stimulation is driven by a condensation mechanism in which the CD28 intracellular domain (ICD) forms signaling condensates with the Src-family kinase Lck. Ligand engagement promotes CD28 ICD accessibility and triggers rapid CD28/Lck condensation, enhancing CD28 phosphorylation, cytoskeletal polarization, and cytokine production. The downstream effectors of CD28, including PI3K and GRB2, can also be recruited into the CD28-Lck condensates in our reconstituted system. We further identify PD-1 as a graded regulator of this process: Monophosphorylated PD-1 is recruited into CD28/Lck condensates, whereas diphosphorylated PD-1 competitively binds the CD28 ICD and dissolves these assemblies. CD28 and PD-1 ICDs also undergo condensation directly, revealing a dynamic and compositionally heterogeneous signaling system. Guided by this competitive condensation mechanism, we engineer CD28 ICD mutants that preserve Lck condensation while resisting PD-1-mediated disruption. Incorporation of these condensation-selective mutants into Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) constructs confers resistance to inhibitory signaling and enhances antitumor efficacy in vivo. These findings establish condensation as a central organizing principle of CD28 costimulation and provide a biophysical framework for engineering more resilient therapeutic T cells.

title: Mitochondrial subpopulations promote cellular responses to changes in metabolic demand and signal transduction
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: When mammalian cells are under increased ATP demand, mitochondria segregate into two distinct subpopulations, one capable of oxidative phosphorylation (oxidative subpopulation) and another specialized in reductive synthesis of metabolic precursors (reductive subpopulation). Here we report that mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) along with protein components of the mitochondrial nucleoid segregate to the oxidative subpopulation in response to increased ATP demand. This suggests that formation of the reductive mitochondrial subpopulation might serve to eliminate alternative uses of mitochondrial NAD(P)H when cells are under bioenergetic or nutrient stress. To examine this further, we studied mitochondria in cells exposed to low levels of glutamine. Mitochondria use glutaminase (GLS1) to maintain net glutamine uptake when cytosolic glutamine decreases, by converting glutamine to glutamate. The resulting glutamate can either be oxidized into α-ketoglutarate to enter the TCA cycle or utilized in the reductive synthesis of proline/ornithine. GLS1 can polymerize into hyperactive filaments in response to elevations in inorganic phosphate as might occur when ATP consumption exceeds production. However, when extracellular glutamine is reduced, GLS1 filaments segregated away from mtDNA, becoming colocalized with pyrroline-5-carboxylate synthase (P5CS) filaments in reductive mitochondria lacking ATP synthase markers. This cosegregation supported the ability of TGF-β signaling to enhance reductive proline/ornithine biosynthesis under low glutamine conditions despite compromising oxidative TCA cycle support from glutamine. The cosegregation of GLS1-P5CS filaments depended on continuing mitochondrial fission/fusion and occurred even in cells lacking mtDNA. Together, these data demonstrate that the reductive mitochondrial subpopulation is functional and under regulation by both metabolic demand and intercellular signal transduction.

title: Multi-omics and spatial analysis of microgravity-grown glioblastoma organoids reveal superior modeling of advanced disease after long-term spaceflight
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Creating accurate organoid models remains a challenge, particularly for diseases like glioblastoma (GBM), an aggressive, treatment-resistant brain cancer with an immunosuppressive microenvironment. To overcome limitations of Earth-based models (sedimentation and disaggregation) and leverage the unique advantages of space (accelerated disease progression and immune dysregulation), this study utilizes a panel of GBM-myeloid organoids cultured for 40 d aboard the International Space Station. Spaceflight-grown GBM organoids have more uniform morphology compared to ground controls. We observed a context-dependent response to spaceflight, with the inclusion of macrophages and monocytes altering the bulk and spatial transcriptional response. While GBM-alone organoids have transcriptional markers of less aggressive disease in microgravity, organoids containing GBM cells + monocytes have increased expression of genes associated with disease progression and poor patient outcomes. Gene expression patterns are more spatially organized, with mesenchymal-related genes enriched in the core and inflammation-related genes enriched at the periphery, mimicking GBM tumor architecture. Microgravity-grown GBM+monocyte organoids exhibit increased secretion of proteins such as CXCL12 and LOX-1, associated with more aggressive disease. Infrared chemical imaging confirms spatial chemical gradients of DNA, protein, and lipid species in both space- and terrestrially-grown organoids. In summary, this work presents not only an advanced model of glioblastoma for basic and translational research but also demonstrates methods to acquire diverse data from organoids compatible with the unique constraints of in-space systems, helping establish a working model for orbital oncology.
